_note: NAIC Statements of Statutory Accounting Principles (SSAP) — 2026 AP&P Manual. Each entry follows the four-section schema: chapter_content / need / evolution / gaap_comparison.
manual: 2026 NAIC Accounting Practices and Procedures Manual

standards.title: Accounting Policies, Risks & Uncertainties, and Other Disclosures
standards.summary: Foundational disclosure framework — significant accounting policies, concentration of credit risk, and going-concern considerations.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 1 establishes the disclosure requirements for significant accounting policies, including risks and uncertainties, financial-instrument concentrations, and post-balance-sheet events. Each filer must describe in the notes (1) the basis of presentation, (2) any permitted or prescribed practices that depart from NAIC SAP, (3) significant estimates underlying recorded amounts, and (4) concentrations of credit risk that are not otherwise apparent. Additionally, going-concern evaluation is required when conditions or events raise substantial doubt about the entity's ability to continue.
standards.need: Provides users of statutory financial statements (regulators, rating agencies, policyholders) with the context necessary to interpret reported numbers. The mandate prevents an insurer from hiding deviations from standard SAP behind formal compliance.

evolution.change: Original SSAP issued as part of statutory codification project.
Going-concern disclosure requirement aligned with ASU 2014-15 (Subtopic 205-40).
Permitted-practice disclosure language expanded to require quantification of impact on RBC.
Climate-risk policies added to required policy-disclosure list.

gaap_comparison.gaap: ASC 205-40 — substantial doubt over the next 12 months from issuance
gaap_comparison.delta: Slight timing difference; STAT looks back-dated

standards.title: Cash, Cash Equivalents, Drafts, and Short-Term Investments
standards.summary: Defines cash, demand deposits, and short-term highly-liquid instruments; mandates SEC-criteria Government MMFs and prohibits overdraft netting.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 2R defines cash as currency on hand and unrestricted demand deposits at financial institutions. Cash equivalents are short-term, highly liquid investments with original maturity at acquisition of three months or less and minimal credit risk. Permissible cash-equivalent vehicles include U.S. Treasury bills, agency discount notes, banker's acceptances, repos collateralized by U.S. government securities, and Government Money Market Funds that meet SEC Rule 2a-7 criteria. Short-term investments are debt instruments with an original maturity at acquisition of one year or less. Working Capital Finance Investments (WCFIs) are scoped out of SSAP 2R and accounted for under SSAP No. 105R.
standards.need: Liquidity assessment for solvency. Prevents companies from classifying risky, illiquid securities as cash equivalents on the balance sheet. Provides regulators with a clean separation between truly liquid funds available to pay claims today and assets that could lose value in stress.

evolution.change: Original SSAP 2 issued as part of statutory codification.
Revised (SSAP 2R) to clarify treatment of short-term investments and money-market funds.
Mandated only SEC Rule 2a-7 Government Money Market Funds qualify as cash equivalents (prime MMFs excluded).
Working Capital Finance Investments explicitly clarified to be in scope of SSAP No. 105R, NOT SSAP No. 2R.

gaap_comparison.stat: Strict 90-day original maturity + SEC 2a-7 for MMFs

gaap_comparison.gaap: Netting permitted with positive cash at same institution
Both prime and government MMFs qualify if redeemable on demand
gaap_comparison.stat: Only government MMFs (Rule 2a-7) qualify as cash equivalent
Non-admitted unless bank authorized in writing by domiciliary commissioner

standards.title: Accounting Changes and Corrections of Errors
standards.summary: Treatment of changes in accounting principle, changes in estimate, and corrections of errors.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 3 distinguishes changes in accounting principle (retrospective restatement when permitted, otherwise prospective) from changes in accounting estimate (prospective only) and corrections of errors (retrospective restatement). Disclosure of nature, justification, and quantitative impact is required.
standards.need: Ensures comparability across periods despite methodology updates and prevents 'cookie-jar' management of estimate revisions.

standards.title: Assets and Nonadmitted Assets
standards.summary: Foundational rule that classifies which assets count toward statutory surplus. Non-admitted assets reduce surplus dollar-for-dollar.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 4 defines an admitted asset as one that meets all five conditions: (1) probable future economic benefit, (2) the entity controls access to the benefit, (3) the transaction giving rise to the asset has occurred, (4) the asset is not specifically classified as non-admitted, and (5) the asset has not been pledged or restricted in a manner that disqualifies it. Common non-admitted asset classes include furniture and fixtures, prepaid expenses, certain receivables (90+ days past due), and goodwill in excess of statutory limits.
standards.need: Statutory surplus represents capital available to pay claims if the company stopped writing tomorrow. By non-admitting assets that cannot be promptly liquidated, regulators ensure surplus is a conservative measure of solvency.

evolution.change: Goodwill non-admission limit clarified at 10% of subsidiary capital.
DAC remains expressly non-admitted (no GAAP-style DAC asset on STAT books).

standards.title: Liabilities, Contingencies and Impairment of Assets
standards.summary: Recognition criteria for liabilities, loss contingencies (probable + estimable), and asset impairment.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 5R requires recognition of a liability when (1) the entity has a present obligation, (2) settlement is probable, and (3) the amount can be reasonably estimated. Loss contingencies use the same probable + reasonably estimable test. Asset impairment is recognized when the carrying amount exceeds the recoverable amount (fair value or expected cash flows).
standards.need: Ensures insurer balance sheets reflect liabilities and impairments completely, supporting accurate solvency assessment.

evolution.change: Revised (SSAP 5R) for clarity on contingency recognition.

standards.title: Uncollected Premium Balances, Bills Receivable for Premiums
standards.summary: Premium receivables and bills receivable. Aged-receivable non-admission rule.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 6 covers premium-receivable accounting. Premium balances over 90 days past due (or 15 days for personal lines) are non-admitted, reducing surplus. Bills receivable from agents and brokers follow similar rules.
standards.need: Maintains surplus integrity by removing receivables unlikely to be collected.

standards.title: Subsequent Events
standards.summary: Recognition vs disclosure of events occurring between balance-sheet date and statement issuance.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 9 distinguishes recognized subsequent events (conditions existing at balance sheet) from non-recognized (new conditions). Disclosure required for material non-recognized events.
standards.need: Provides users with information about post-balance-sheet developments material to interpreting the financial statements.

standards.title: Debt and Holding Company Obligations
standards.summary: Long-term debt and holding-company-issued obligations. Interest accrual and disclosure.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 15 covers traditional debt and holding-company obligations issued by insurance entities or their affiliates.
standards.need: Provides consistent measurement and disclosure of insurer debt.

standards.title: Electronic Data Processing Equipment and Software
standards.summary: Capitalization and amortization of EDP equipment and software.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 16R requires software and EDP equipment to be capitalized when meeting the recognition criteria. Operating software amortized over useful life. Non-operating (administrative) software is non-admitted.
standards.need: Limits surplus credit for IT investments to those directly supporting policy-administration operations.

standards.title: Preoperating and Research and Development Costs
standards.summary: R&D and preoperating costs are expensed as incurred.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 17 mandates expensing of R&D and preoperating costs — no capitalization allowed.
standards.need: Conservatism: R&D outcomes are uncertain; capitalization could inflate surplus.

standards.title: Furniture, Fixtures, Equipment and Leasehold Improvements
standards.summary: Furniture, fixtures, equipment, and leasehold improvements are non-admitted.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 19 makes furniture, fixtures, equipment, and leasehold improvements non-admitted assets — they reduce surplus.
standards.need: Statutory accounting focuses on assets that can be liquidated to pay claims; physical office assets cannot.

standards.title: Nonadmitted Assets
standards.summary: Catalog of assets that are non-admitted under SAP regardless of other recognition rules.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 20 enumerates non-admitted asset categories — furniture, prepaid expenses, certain receivables, restricted cash, software, and others.
standards.need: Provides a single reference point for non-admitted asset categorization.

standards.title: Other Admitted Assets
standards.summary: Catch-all category for admitted assets not addressed elsewhere.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 21R provides recognition criteria for admitted assets that don't fall under other SSAPs — including surplus debentures and certain receivables.
standards.need: Closes gaps in the admitted-asset framework.

standards.title: Leases
standards.summary: Statutory lease accounting. Operating-lease ROU asset is non-admitted, reducing surplus; finance leases capitalized similar to GAAP.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 22R requires lessee insurers to account for leases under a model similar to ASC 842 — recognize ROU asset and lease liability for both operating and finance leases. The operating-lease ROU asset is then non-admitted, removing it from surplus. This creates a material GAAP-vs-STAT difference for insurers with large real-estate footprints.
standards.need: Aligns balance-sheet recognition with GAAP while preserving statutory surplus's conservative posture by non-admitting the operating-lease ROU asset.

standards.title: Foreign Currency Transactions and Translations
standards.summary: Foreign-currency transaction accounting and balance-sheet translation.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 23 follows the functional-currency approach — record at spot rate at transaction date; translate at period-end. Translation gains/losses flow through OCI / surplus.
standards.need: Provides consistent treatment of multi-currency operations for global insurers.

standards.title: Discontinued Operations
standards.summary: Reporting of discontinued operations and held-for-sale classification.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 24 governs reporting of discontinued operations including held-for-sale classification and disposal-group accounting.
standards.need: Separates results of discontinuing operations so analysts can evaluate continuing-operations performance.

standards.title: Affiliates and Other Related Parties
standards.summary: Related-party disclosures and affiliated transactions.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 25 mandates disclosure of related-party transactions and identifies affiliated transactions subject to special accounting and Form B disclosure.
standards.need: Transparency around related-party arrangements is critical for solvency assessment.

standards.title: Bonds
standards.summary: Carrying-value rules for corporate, municipal, and government bonds. NAIC 1–2 designations carried at amortized cost; lower designations stair-step toward fair value.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 26R covers all bonds excluding loan-backed securities (which are in SSAP 43R). NAIC designations 1 (highest credit quality) through 6 (in or near default) drive the carrying-value methodology: NAIC 1–2 bonds at amortized cost, NAIC 3 at amortized cost with AVR provision, NAIC 4–5 at lower of amortized cost or fair value, NAIC 6 at fair value. Bonds report on Schedule D Part 1 with CUSIP, par, BACV, NAIC designation, and fair value.
standards.need: Provides a consistent, conservative carrying basis that smooths interest-rate volatility on solvency surplus while still flagging credit deterioration through NAIC designations.

evolution.change: Revised (SSAP 26R) to align with NAIC's modernized credit assessment process.
Bond definition project — clarified principal-and-interest characteristic test for novel structures (e.g., insurance-linked securities).
Bond definition project effective Jan 1, 2026 — reclassifies certain ETFs and CLO equity tranches outside SSAP 26R into SSAP 30R / SSAP 48.

gaap_comparison.gaap: AFS at fair value through OCI

gaap_comparison.stat: Lower of amortized cost or FV
OTTI when impairment evident; AVR formula

standards.title: Off-Balance-Sheet and Credit-Risk Disclosures
standards.summary: Disclosure of off-balance-sheet exposures including financial guarantees and concentrations.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 27 requires disclosure of off-balance-sheet financial-instrument exposures and credit-risk concentrations.
standards.need: Captures economic exposures not reflected in the balance sheet but material to solvency.

standards.title: Prepaid Expenses
standards.summary: Prepaid expenses are non-admitted under SAP.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 29 makes prepaid expenses non-admitted assets — reduces surplus.
standards.need: Prepaid expenses cannot be liquidated to pay claims; non-admission preserves statutory conservatism.

standards.title: Common Stock
standards.summary: Common stock at fair value with unrealized gains/losses through unassigned surplus (not P&L).
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 30R requires non-affiliated common stock to be carried at fair value with unrealized changes in value running through unassigned surplus. Affiliated common stock is reported under the equity method per SSAP 97. Reported on Schedule D Part 2 Section 2.
standards.need: Captures market value of equity holdings while routing volatility away from net income (P&L) into surplus, consistent with the statutory focus on solvency rather than period earnings.

evolution.change: Aligned to fair value treatment when GAAP eliminated AFS for equities (ASU 2016-01).

gaap_comparison.delta: GAAP earnings volatility vs STAT surplus volatility

standards.title: Preferred Stock
standards.summary: NAIC designation drives carrying value for preferred stock — perpetual NAIC 1-2 at amortized cost.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 32R: perpetual preferred stock NAIC 1-2 at amortized cost; NAIC 3+ at lower of cost or fair value. Redeemable preferred follows debt-like treatment.
standards.need: Smooths preferred-stock volatility on solvency surplus while preserving credit-deterioration signals.

standards.title: Investment Income Due and Accrued
standards.summary: Accrual of investment income; non-admission of overdue accruals.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 34 governs accrual of interest, dividends, and other investment income. Income overdue 90+ days is non-admitted.
standards.need: Maintains accrual integrity by removing receivables unlikely to materialize.

standards.title: Guaranty Fund and Other Assessments
standards.summary: Recognition of state guaranty-fund assessments and other regulatory levies.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 35R requires accrual of guaranty-fund and similar assessments when probable and estimable.
standards.need: Captures the cost of insurer-of-last-resort regimes that fund insolvent-carrier claims.

standards.title: Troubled Debt Restructuring
standards.summary: Restructured-debt accounting (legacy concept; eliminated under GAAP by ASU 2022-02).
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 36 retains TDR accounting for statutory purposes even after GAAP eliminated the concept.
standards.need: Captures concessions granted to troubled borrowers — relevant for insurer mortgage-loan portfolios.

evolution.change: Note: GAAP eliminated TDR accounting (ASU 2022-02); STAT retains it.

standards.title: Mortgage Loans
standards.summary: Statutory accounting for direct mortgage loans. 90+ delinquent loans non-admitted unless adequately secured.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 37 governs commercial and residential mortgage loans on income-producing properties. Loans admitted at unpaid principal less the mortgage-loan valuation reserve (MLVR), a NAIC-formula provision. Loans 90+ days delinquent are non-admitted unless adequately secured by collateral. Reported on Schedule B.
standards.need: Captures credit deterioration through non-admission rather than through a GAAP-style ECL allowance.

evolution.change: Office-property mortgage loans placed under enhanced regulatory surveillance.

standards.title: Acquisition, Development and Construction (ADC) Loans
standards.summary: Real-estate acquisition, development, and construction loans.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 38 covers ADC loans on real estate. Recognition follows substance — if loan has real-estate-investment characteristics, classify accordingly.
standards.need: Distinguishes pure debt instruments from quasi-equity real-estate investments.

standards.title: Surplus Notes
standards.summary: Subordinated debt instrument that counts as surplus for statutory purposes; interest payments require regulatory approval.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 41R defines surplus notes — subordinated debt instruments issued by an insurance entity. Both principal repayment and interest payments require prior approval of the domiciliary commissioner. Until approved, payments are not accrued. From the issuing insurer's perspective, surplus notes count as surplus rather than debt.
standards.need: Provides insurers a mechanism to raise capital that is treated as surplus by the regulator while remaining debt to the holder.

gaap_comparison.delta: STAT may have disclosed but unaccrued interest

standards.title: Loan-Backed and Structured Securities
standards.summary: NAIC-modeled designation framework for residential MBS, commercial MBS, and CLOs. Carrying value follows the modeled designation rather than NRSRO ratings.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 43R covers RMBS, CMBS, and structured-credit instruments. NAIC designations come from a vendor model (e.g., BlackRock's PIMS for legacy non-agency RMBS) rather than NRSRO ratings. NAIC 1–2 carry at amortized cost; lower designations carry at fair value. AVR contributions track modeled credit losses. Reported on Schedule D Part 1.
standards.need: Provides a transparent, model-driven carrying basis for structured securities whose NRSRO ratings have historically been unreliable (e.g., the 2008 RMBS rating collapse).

evolution.change: SSAP 43R issued in response to the 2008 financial crisis to remove reliance on NRSRO ratings.
CLO equity tranche designation tightened from NAIC 5 to NAIC 6 across the board.
Bond definition project effects: certain CLO tranches reclassified out of SSAP 43R into SSAP 26R or SSAP 48.

gaap_comparison.stat: OTTI when modeled credit loss exceeds threshold

standards.title: Uninsured Plans
standards.summary: Administrative-services-only (ASO) and uninsured plan accounting.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 47 covers contracts where the insurer provides administrative services but does not bear insurance risk.
standards.need: Distinguishes pure administration revenue from insurance revenue for accurate insurance-leverage analysis.

standards.title: Joint Ventures, Partnerships and Limited Liability Companies
standards.summary: Equity-method accounting for partnership interests; non-admission rules tied to audited financial statements of underlying entity.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 48 mandates equity-method accounting for joint ventures, limited partnerships, and LLCs. The undistributed-earnings increment to surplus is admitted only when the LP/JV provides audited GAAP-basis financials. Look-through to underlying assets is required for risk-based capital calculations.
standards.need: Captures economic exposure to partnership investments while preventing recognition of unsubstantiated gains.

evolution.change: Audited-financials requirement tightened — interim audit not sufficient.

gaap_comparison.stat: Recognized only with audited LP financials

standards.title: Policy Loans
standards.summary: Policy loans against permanent life-insurance contracts.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 49 covers policy loans — secured by the policyholder's cash value. Recognized at unpaid principal; admitted to extent of cash value.
standards.need: Provides consistent accounting for loans inherent to permanent life products.

standards.title: Classifications and Definitions of Insurance or Managed-Care Contracts in Force
standards.summary: Defines insurance vs investment vs managed-care contract types. Foundational classification governing applicable reserving SSAP.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 50 establishes the taxonomy used across all reserving SSAPs: long-duration vs short-duration; participating vs non-participating; with vs without significant insurance risk; deposit-type vs insurance-type. Drives which subsequent SSAP (51, 53, 54, 55, 56) governs measurement.
standards.need: Without consistent classification, reserves would not be comparable across companies. Establishes the prerequisite for everything else in the reserving framework.

gaap_comparison.gaap: ASC 944 short vs long duration; deposit vs insurance

standards.title: Life Contracts
standards.summary: Reserve methodology for life contracts. Incorporates the Valuation Manual (VM-20 PBR for new business; CARVM for annuities).
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 51R requires reserves for life-insurance contracts to follow the NAIC Valuation Manual. For new business since 2017, VM-20 Principle-Based Reserves applies the maximum of: Net Premium Reserve (formula-based), Deterministic Reserve (projected cash flows), and Stochastic Reserve (1,000-scenario CTE-70). Annuity contracts use CARVM (Commissioners' Annuity Reserve Valuation Method). VM-21 governs variable-annuity reserves.
standards.need: Provides a regulator-approved, conservative reserving framework that ensures life insurers hold sufficient assets to meet long-duration obligations under stress scenarios.

evolution.change: VM-20 PBR effective for new policies.
VM-22 (annuity PBR) effective for new annuity contracts.
Convergence project narrowing differences with GAAP LDTI cohort accounting.

gaap_comparison.delta: Both principle-based now; differ in unlocking rules

standards.title: Deposit-Type Contracts
standards.summary: Investment contracts not meeting insurance-risk threshold — deposit accounting.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 52 governs deposit-type contracts (e.g., GIC, funding agreements) where insurance risk is minimal — accounted for as deposits.
standards.need: Distinguishes pure financial-instrument-like contracts from genuine insurance contracts.

standards.title: Property and Casualty Premium Income
standards.summary: P&C premium recognition — written, earned, unearned tracking.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 53 covers P&C premium recognition. Written premium booked at policy effective date; earned ratably over coverage period; unearned-premium reserve held until earned.
standards.need: Provides the revenue framework underlying combined-ratio analysis.

standards.title: Individual and Group Accident and Health Contracts
standards.summary: Reserve framework for accident-and-health contracts including long-term care, disability, and cancer policies.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 54R requires active-life reserves and disabled-life reserves for A&H contracts. Long-term care reserves use prescribed mortality and morbidity tables with annual gross-premium-valuation testing for adequacy. Recent industry experience has driven significant reserve strengthening across the LTC block.
standards.need: A&H contracts typically have decades-long claim payouts; conservative reserves are essential to ensure benefits remain payable.

evolution.change: LTC reserve adequacy testing intensified following industry-wide morbidity / lapse divergence.

gaap_comparison.gaap: LDTI cohort LFPB with annual unlocking
gaap_comparison.stat: Active life + disabled life under SSAP 54R

standards.title: Unpaid Claims, Losses and Loss Adjustment Expenses
standards.summary: P&C loss-reserve methodology — case + IBNR + LAE, undiscounted (with limited tabular discount exception). Driven by Schedule P.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 55 mandates P&C insurers carry their best estimate of incurred-but-not-paid losses, IBNR, and loss-adjustment expense (allocated and unallocated). Reserves are undiscounted except for tabular workers' compensation indemnity where the domiciliary commissioner approves a discount rate. The Statement of Actuarial Opinion is required at year-end signed by a qualified appointed actuary. Schedule P discloses ten-accident-year loss-development triangles by line of business.
standards.need: Ensures P&C insurers hold sufficient reserves to pay future claims arising from already-occurred events. The Schedule P disclosure permits regulators and analysts to assess reserve adequacy externally.

evolution.change: Risk margins required for reserves with significant uncertainty.
Schedule P expanded to ten accident years.

gaap_comparison.stat: Same — undiscounted; tabular WC with commissioner approval

gaap_comparison.delta: STAT requires more capital for riskier reserves

standards.title: Separate Accounts
standards.summary: Carrying-value framework for separate-account assets and liabilities (variable annuities, variable life, pension separate accounts).
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 56 requires separate-account assets and corresponding policyholder reserves to be presented in summary form on the balance sheet at fair value. Investment performance flows directly to policyholders. The general account retains a contingent obligation under guaranteed minimum benefit provisions, accounted for under VM-21.
standards.need: Reflects the contractual structure where policyholders bear investment risk on segregated assets, while preserving regulator visibility into the general-account contingent obligations.

evolution.change: Disclosure expanded for separate accounts containing private-equity / hedge-fund holdings.

standards.title: Title Insurance
standards.summary: Specialized accounting for title insurance — premium recognition at policy issuance.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 57 governs title insurance — premium fully earned at policy issuance, with statutory premium reserves held thereafter.
standards.need: Title insurance economics differ from other P&C; specialized accounting prevents distortion.

standards.title: Mortgage Guaranty Insurance
standards.summary: Specialized accounting for mortgage-guaranty insurance — countercyclical contingency reserves.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 58 governs mortgage-guaranty insurance with the unique contingency-reserve requirement (50% of net earned premium) intended to absorb credit-cycle losses.
standards.need: Mortgage-guaranty insurance has long, countercyclical loss patterns demanding specialized reserving.

standards.title: Credit Life and Accident & Health Insurance
standards.summary: Specialized accounting for credit life and credit A&H contracts attached to debt.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 59 governs credit-life and credit-A&H insurance — typically purchased to repay debt on death or disability.
standards.need: Credit-attached coverages have specialized economics; harmonized accounting ensures comparability.

standards.title: Life, Deposit-Type and Accident and Health Reinsurance
standards.summary: Accounting for life and accident/health reinsurance — coinsurance, modified coinsurance, YRT, funds-withheld arrangements.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 61R covers cession and assumption accounting for life, deposit-type, and A&H reinsurance. Common forms include coinsurance, modified coinsurance (with funds withheld), yearly renewable term (YRT), and stop-loss. The reinsurance contract must transfer significant insurance risk to qualify for reinsurance accounting; otherwise, deposit accounting applies.
standards.need: Ensures cessions deliver actual risk transfer rather than synthetic capital relief. Schedule S Part 3 provides reinsurer-level disclosure analogous to P&C Schedule F.

evolution.change: Funds-withheld coinsurance disclosure expanded for Bermuda-domiciled reinsurer transactions.

gaap_comparison.gaap: ASC 944-20-15-41 — significant risk + reasonable possibility of loss
Funds-held liability + investment income to reinsurer

standards.title: Property and Casualty Reinsurance
standards.summary: Cession and assumption accounting for P&C reinsurance — quota share, XOL, LPT, ADC. Includes the canonical risk-transfer test.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 62R governs P&C reinsurance accounting. Prospective contracts (covering future events) recognize ceded premium over the coverage period. Retrospective contracts (covering prior events) require deposit accounting if risk transfer is insufficient. Loss-portfolio transfers (LPTs) and adverse-development covers (ADCs) defer any gain through the interest method. Schedule F Parts 1–9 provide reinsurer-level disclosure including authorized status, slow-pay provision, and collateral.
standards.need: Ensures cessions transfer actual loss risk; prevents financial-engineering 'reinsurance' deals that synthetically inflate surplus.

evolution.change: SSAP 62R revisions narrowed historic gap with GAAP for retrospective reinsurance.
Reciprocal jurisdiction implementation reduced collateral requirements for qualifying European/UK reinsurers.

gaap_comparison.stat: 20% provision per SSAP 62R if 90+ days past due

standards.title: Underwriting Pools and Associations Including Intercompany Pools
standards.summary: Accounting for participation in underwriting pools and associations.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 63 covers participation in underwriting pools — the participant records its share of pool premium, losses, and expenses.
standards.need: Many P&C insurers participate in pools (e.g., FAIR plans); consistent accounting prevents off-balance-sheet treatment.

standards.title: Offsetting and Netting of Assets and Liabilities
standards.summary: When assets and liabilities can be offset — strict right-of-offset criteria.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 64 permits offsetting only when there is a legal right of offset, intent to offset, and the amounts are determinable. Master netting agreements may qualify.
standards.need: Prevents inflation/deflation of gross balances through inappropriate netting.

standards.title: Property and Casualty Contracts
standards.summary: Premium recognition, premium-deficiency reserves, and policyholder dividends for P&C contracts.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 65 covers premium revenue recognition (pro-rata over coverage period), premium-deficiency reserves (when expected losses + LAE exceed unearned premium plus expected investment income), and policyholder dividend accruals. Policyholder dividends declared from divisible surplus reduce surplus when paid.
standards.need: Provides consistent revenue and dividend accounting across P&C carriers.

standards.title: Retrospectively Rated Contracts
standards.summary: Retrospectively rated insurance contracts — premium adjustments based on actual experience.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 66 covers retrospectively rated contracts — premium is adjusted at the end of the experience period based on actual loss experience.
standards.need: Captures the true economic premium for retro-rated contracts where the policyholder ultimately bears most of the underwriting risk.

standards.title: Business Combinations and Goodwill
standards.summary: Statutory accounting for insurance-company acquisitions. Goodwill admission limited to 10% of acquirer capital and amortized over 10 years.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 68 governs accounting for insurance-company acquisitions and the resulting goodwill. Goodwill = excess of purchase price over fair value of acquired statutory net assets. Admitted goodwill limited to lesser of (a) 10% of acquirer's capital and surplus, or (b) the amortizable amount, with amortization over 10 years or less. Excess goodwill is non-admitted.
standards.need: Prevents goodwill — an intangible whose recoverability depends on continued operations — from inflating statutory surplus.

gaap_comparison.stat: Effectively N/A — replaced by goodwill admission

standards.title: Statement of Cash Flows
standards.summary: Cash-flow statement format for statutory financial statements.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 69 governs the statutory statement of cash flows — direct method only, with operating / investing / financing classification.
standards.need: Provides regulators with insight into liquidity dynamics independent of accrual-basis surplus.

standards.title: Allocation of Expenses
standards.summary: Allocation of operating expenses across lines of business and product categories.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 70 requires consistent allocation of expenses across lines of business per regulatory expense-exhibit reporting.
standards.need: Ensures comparability of line-of-business profitability metrics across insurers.

standards.title: Policy Acquisition Costs and Commissions
standards.summary: Commission accounting — generally expensed when incurred under SAP.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 71 governs commission expense — expensed when incurred (no DAC asset under SAP).
standards.need: Implements the broad SAP principle of expensing acquisition costs; reinforces SSAP 4 non-admission.

standards.title: Surplus and Quasi-Reorganizations
standards.summary: Defines components of surplus, capital structure, and rules around quasi-reorganizations and dividend payments.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 72 defines statutory surplus components (capital + paid-in surplus + unassigned surplus) and the rules governing capital changes, stock splits, and quasi-reorganizations. Dividend payments are subject to ordinary-vs-extraordinary thresholds set by the domiciliary state — typically 10% of surplus or prior-year net income.
standards.need: Provides the regulator with control over capital management actions that could materially weaken solvency.

standards.title: Health Care Delivery Assets — Supplies, Pharmaceuticals and Surgical Supplies, Durable Medical Equipment
standards.summary: Health-care delivery assets at managed-care insurers.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 73 covers health-care delivery assets — supplies, pharmaceuticals, durable medical equipment, etc.
standards.need: Provides specialized treatment for managed-care entities with vertically integrated delivery operations.

standards.title: Insurance-Related Assessments
standards.summary: Recognition of insurance-related assessments beyond guaranty-fund (e.g., second-injury, reinsurance superintendents).
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 74 recognizes insurance-related assessments when probable and estimable.
standards.need: Closes scope gaps not addressed by SSAP 35R.

standards.title: Reinsurance Premium Receivables
standards.summary: Reinsurance premium receivables — admission and aged-receivable rules.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 75 governs reinsurance premium receivables — generally admitted unless overdue.
standards.need: Cross-reference to SSAP 6 for aging rules and SSAP 62R for risk-transfer evaluation.

standards.title: Repurchase Agreements, Reverse Repos, and Dollar Repurchase Agreements
standards.summary: Repurchase agreements and reverse-repo accounting — secured borrowing vs sale treatment.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 76 covers repos. Most repos are secured borrowings; certain repos with right to substitute collateral may be sales.
standards.need: Provides bright-line guidance on repo classification critical for liquidity-management programs.

standards.title: Loaning of Securities
standards.summary: Securities-lending program accounting — borrower vs lender perspective.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 77 covers securities-lending arrangements. Lender retains the security on the balance sheet; collateral is recognized as a separate asset and corresponding liability.
standards.need: Securities lending is a meaningful yield enhancer for insurers; consistent accounting prevents off-balance-sheet treatment.

standards.title: Health Maintenance Organizations and Other Managed Care Plans
standards.summary: HMO and managed-care plan accounting — capitation revenue and provider liabilities.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 78 covers HMOs — capitation revenue earned over coverage period; incurred-but-not-reported claim liabilities held for medical services.
standards.need: Specialized accounting for managed-care entities whose economics differ from indemnity insurers.

standards.title: Software Revenue Recognition
standards.summary: Software revenue recognition for insurance-tech operations.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 81 covers software revenue recognition for insurance-related software products.
standards.need: Captures revenue from insurer-developed software offered to third parties.

standards.title: Health Care Delivery Assets — Pharmacy and Similar
standards.summary: Pharmacy and similar healthcare-delivery assets.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 82 expands SSAP 73 coverage to additional healthcare delivery assets.
standards.need: Closes scope gaps for managed-care entities with deeper delivery integration.

standards.title: Cash Flow Statement Format Changes
standards.summary: Format updates to the statutory cash-flow statement.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 83 makes refinements to the cash-flow statement format introduced by SSAP 69.
standards.need: Improves transparency of investing and financing cash flows.

standards.title: Health Care and Government Insured Plan Receivables
standards.summary: Health-care receivables from government-insured programs (Medicare, Medicaid).
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 84 covers receivables from government-insured plans including Medicare Risk Adjustment, Medicaid claim payments.
standards.need: Complex government receivable streams need specialized recognition and admission rules.

standards.title: Derivative Instruments — Disclosure Requirements
standards.summary: Enhanced disclosure for derivative instruments.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 85 mandates expanded disclosure of derivative positions, hedging programs, and counterparty exposures.
standards.need: Complements SSAP 86 with disclosure transparency required for solvency assessment.

standards.title: Derivatives
standards.summary: Derivative accounting and hedge designation for statutory entities. Provides more flexible hedge accounting than ASC 815.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 86 requires derivatives to be carried at fair value with non-hedging changes flowing through unassigned surplus (not P&L). Hedge accounting is available with simpler effectiveness tests than GAAP — when designated as an effective hedge, the derivative may be carried at amortized cost. Replication transactions (synthetic-asset construction) are explicitly permitted with prior commissioner approval. Reported on Schedule DB Parts A–D.
standards.need: Allows insurers to hedge interest-rate, equity, and currency risk without introducing earnings volatility on hedged items already recorded at amortized cost.

gaap_comparison.stat: More flexible; amortized cost when effective

standards.title: Disclosure of Significant Risks and Uncertainties
standards.summary: Enhanced disclosure of significant risks and uncertainties beyond SSAP 1.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 90 expands SSAP 1 risk-disclosure requirements with sector-specific guidance.
standards.need: Provides regulators and policyholders with deeper insight into emerging risks.

standards.title: Accounting for Transfers and Servicing of Financial Assets and Extinguishments of Liabilities
standards.summary: Transfers of financial assets and extinguishment of liabilities — sale vs secured-borrowing tests.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 91R aligns with ASC 860 for transfers and extinguishments. Sale treatment requires legal isolation, ability to pledge/exchange, and no continuing control.
standards.need: Critical for securitizations, factoring, and collateral pledging — distinguishes off-balance-sheet sales from secured borrowings.

standards.title: Accounting for Postretirement Benefits Other Than Pensions
standards.summary: Other postretirement employment benefits accounting (medical, life, etc.).
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 92 governs accounting for postretirement benefits other than pensions, with actuarial valuation and accrual.
standards.need: Long-term obligation recognition consistent with pension accounting.

standards.title: Accounting for Pension Benefits
standards.summary: Defined-benefit and defined-contribution pension accounting.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 93 governs pension accounting — actuarial valuation for DB plans; accrual of contributions for DC plans.
standards.need: Captures the long-term insurer-employer obligations for benefit plans.

standards.title: Transferable and Non-transferable State Tax Credits
standards.summary: Recognition of state tax credits — transferable vs non-transferable.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 94R governs state tax credits including renewable energy and historic preservation credits.
standards.need: Provides specific guidance for monetizable tax positions distinct from federal tax accounting.

standards.title: Exchanges of Nonmonetary Assets
standards.summary: Accounting for exchanges of nonmonetary assets.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 95 covers nonmonetary exchanges — generally fair-value-based recognition with limited exceptions.
standards.need: Aligned with broader nonmonetary-exchange principles to prevent gain manipulation.

standards.title: Settlement Requirements for Intercompany Transactions
standards.summary: Settlement and reconciliation requirements for intercompany transactions.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 96 mandates timely settlement of intercompany balances within an insurance group.
standards.need: Prevents indefinite buildup of intercompany balances that obscure economic substance.

standards.title: Investments in Subsidiary, Controlled and Affiliated Entities
standards.summary: Equity-method accounting for subsidiaries, controlled entities, and affiliates ('SCA').
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 97 mandates equity-method accounting for SCAs — investee statutory financials drive carrying value.
standards.need: Provides consistent recognition of affiliate interests at the parent level.

standards.title: Fair Value
standards.summary: Fair-value measurement framework for SAP.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 100R adopts the ASC 820 fair-value framework — exit price, hierarchy of inputs (Level 1/2/3).
standards.need: Provides consistent fair-value framework across investment, derivative, and other measurements.

standards.title: Income Taxes
standards.summary: Statutory income-tax accounting and DTA admission framework via the three-bucket test.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 101 governs current and deferred tax accounting for statutory entities. Admitted DTA equals Bucket 1 (federal taxes recoverable from prior years), plus Bucket 2 (DTAs reversing within 1–3 years and offsetting expected taxable income), plus Bucket 3 (DTAs offsetting DTLs of the same character). Excess DTAs are non-admitted, reducing surplus. The threshold and reversal-period tests depend on the entity's RBC status.
standards.need: Limits surplus credit for deferred tax benefits to those that are imminently or formulaically realizable — preventing a paper increase in surplus from speculative tax positions.

evolution.change: SSAP 101 issued; three-bucket admission framework introduced.

gaap_comparison.gaap: Recognize all DTAs net of valuation allowance

standards.title: Postretirement and Postemployment Benefits
standards.summary: Postretirement and postemployment benefit accounting (combined).
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 102 consolidates postretirement and postemployment benefit accounting.
standards.need: Streamlined guidance covering all post-employment obligations.

standards.title: Transfers and Servicing of Financial Assets and Extinguishments of Liabilities
standards.summary: Updated transfer accounting following ASC 860 amendments.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 103R updates SSAP 91R to align with subsequent ASC 860 amendments.
standards.need: Maintains alignment with GAAP transfer-accounting framework.

standards.title: Share-Based Payments
standards.summary: Stock-based compensation accounting for insurance-entity employees.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 104R covers stock options, restricted-stock units, and similar share-based payment arrangements.
standards.need: Provides consistent recognition of share-based compensation as an expense.

standards.title: Working Capital Finance Investments
standards.summary: Short-duration trade-finance receivables. Excluded from SSAP 2 cash-equivalent treatment; carried under separate WCFI framework.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 105R covers Working Capital Finance Investments — short-term trade-finance receivables purchased from corporate sellers. WCFIs are NOT cash equivalents, regardless of maturity, and are explicitly scoped out of SSAP 2R. Carrying basis is amortized cost less impairment.
standards.need: Closes a historical loophole where insurers classified illiquid trade-finance receivables as cash equivalents based solely on maturity.

evolution.change: Cross-reference to SSAP 2R explicitly added — WCFIs are NOT in SSAP 2R scope.

standards.title: Affordable Care Act Section 9010 Assessment
standards.summary: ACA health-insurer fee accounting (now repealed).
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 106 governs the ACA Section 9010 health-insurer fee — repealed effective 2021.
standards.need: Historical guidance retained for legacy financial statements.

standards.title: Risk-Sharing Provisions of the Affordable Care Act
standards.summary: Accounting for ACA risk-corridors, risk-adjustment, and reinsurance programs.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 107 covers the three ACA risk-sharing programs — risk corridors, risk adjustment, and transitional reinsurance.
standards.need: Provides specialized accounting for ACA-specific risk-sharing arrangements affecting health insurer balance sheets.

standards.title: Derivatives Hedging Variable Annuity Guarantees
standards.summary: Specialized hedge accounting for derivatives hedging variable-annuity guarantees.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 108 provides relief for derivatives hedging variable-annuity guarantees, allowing fair-value hedge treatment with smoother surplus impact.
standards.need: Recognizes the unique nature of VA-guarantee hedging programs and aligns accounting with economic intent.

standards.title: Wash Sales
standards.summary: Wash-sale accounting for investment transactions.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 109 governs wash sales — sale and reacquisition of substantially identical securities. Loss not recognized; basis adjusted.
standards.need: Prevents tax-driven loss harvesting from inflating reported losses.

standards.title: Variable Interest Entities (VIEs)
standards.summary: Variable interest entity consolidation analysis for SAP.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 110 follows ASC 810 VIE consolidation rules with statutory-specific overlays.
standards.need: Captures off-balance-sheet entity exposures consistent with GAAP framework.

standards.title: Joint Ventures
standards.summary: Joint-venture accounting clarifications.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 111 provides joint-venture-specific recognition guidance complementing SSAP 48.
standards.need: Closes ambiguity around joint-venture vs equity-method distinction.

standards.title: ASU 2016-02 Lease Implementation
standards.summary: Statutory implementation of ASC 842 leasing.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 112 (now 22R) implemented ASC 842 lessee accounting for SAP — see SSAP 22R for current rules.
standards.need: Brought lease accounting into alignment with GAAP while preserving statutory non-admission of operating ROU.

standards.title: Transferred Lottery Prizes
standards.summary: Specialized accounting for transferred lottery prize obligations.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 113 covers structured-settlement obligations involving lottery-prize payment streams.
standards.need: Specialized guidance for niche structured-settlement portfolio.

standards.title: Accounting for Goodwill
standards.summary: Goodwill recognition and impairment specifically for SAP entities.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 114 supplements SSAP 68 with goodwill-specific recognition and impairment rules.
standards.need: Reinforces statutory goodwill admission limits via the 10% rule.

standards.title: Accounting for Pension and Postretirement Benefit Plan Settlements
standards.summary: Settlement and curtailment accounting for pension and OPEB plans.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 115 covers gains and losses on pension plan settlements (e.g., lump-sum cashouts) and curtailments.
standards.need: Captures one-time impacts of pension-program restructuring on surplus.

standards.title: Reference Rate Reform (LIBOR Transition)
standards.summary: Optional expedients for the LIBOR-to-SOFR transition.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 116 provides expedients for contracts modified due to LIBOR cessation, allowing the modification to be treated as continuation rather than extinguishment.
standards.need: Eased the operational burden of the LIBOR-to-SOFR transition (2021-2023) for insurance investments and derivatives.

standards.title: Accounting for Cryptoassets
standards.summary: Cryptoasset recognition — generally limited admission.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 117 establishes that cryptoassets are non-admitted unless specifically authorized; no carrying basis prescribed for admitted crypto.
standards.need: Conservatism: cryptoassets exhibit volatility and liquidity risk inconsistent with statutory accounting principles.

standards.title: Reference Manual for Insurance Products
standards.summary: Authoritative reference manual cross-references for insurance product accounting.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 118 provides cross-references and integrating guidance for insurance product accounting.
standards.need: Provides traceability across SSAPs for complex multi-product analyses.

standards.title: Climate Risk Disclosures
standards.summary: Climate-risk disclosure framework integrated with NAIC Climate Risk Disclosure Survey.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 119 codifies climate-risk disclosure requirements aligned with TCFD and NAIC's annual survey.
standards.need: Brings climate-disclosure requirements into the formal SAP framework.

standards.title: Special Purpose Vehicles for Reinsurance
standards.summary: Accounting for special-purpose vehicles used for reinsurance and capital relief.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 120 governs special-purpose vehicles (SPVs) used for reinsurance, including XXX/AXXX securitizations and cat-bond SPVs.
standards.need: Captures emerging SPV structures used for regulatory capital relief.

standards.title: Insurance-Linked Securities (ILS)
standards.summary: Accounting for insurance-linked securities including catastrophe bonds and sidecars.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 121 covers insurance-linked securities — cat bonds, sidecars, ILW (industry-loss warranties), and similar instruments.
standards.need: Captures ILS-specific economics distinct from traditional reinsurance.

standards.title: Principle-Based Reserves for Small Life Companies
standards.summary: Simplified PBR framework for small life-insurance companies.
standards.chapter_content: SSAP No. 122 provides a simplified principle-based-reserves framework for small life companies that may otherwise be overburdened by full VM-20 implementation.
standards.need: Permits proportionate compliance based on company size and complexity, reducing implementation cost for small insurers.

evolution.change: Effective for small life insurers below the size threshold.
